summary: Preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executes bundled obfuscated payload via downloaded Bun
details: Package @servicetitan/json-render-react@0.4.7 declares a preinstall script `node setup.mjs` that downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from oven-sh's GitHub releases, extracts and chmods the bun binary, and then executes a bundled 727KB heavily obfuscated JavaScript file (math_init.js) via `execFileSync(bunPath, [math_init.js])`. math_init.js is a single-line file with obfuscator.io fingerprints (string-array rotation function performing push(shift()) over a ~1000-entry decode table, hex identifiers) and is unrelated to the package's advertised purpose (a React JSON-render UI catalog); no code in the shipped React bundle references it. The preinstall launcher setup.mjs is itself obfuscated with hex-mangled identifiers (_0x488df8, _0x52943e) and string-property dispatch tables, which a plain runtime-download script would not need. Fetching an alternate runtime specifically to execute an opaque obfuscated sibling file at install time is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: it runs arbitrary attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine during `npm install`, and using Bun to execute the payload bypasses Node-based install-time scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
